description: Galbi, also known as Korean BBQ Short Ribs, is a beloved dish featuring tender, marinated beef short ribs grilled to perfection. The ribs are infused with a sweet and savory sauce, creating an irresistible caramelized crust and juicy interior. This iconic Korean recipe brings authentic flavors and a delightful dining experience to your home.

instructions.title: Prepare the Short Ribs
instructions.text: Rinse the flanken-cut short ribs under cold water to remove any bone fragments. Pat them thoroughly dry with paper towels. You can optionally make small slits in the meat between the bones to help the marinade penetrate deeper.

instructions.title: Make the Galbi Marinade
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the soy sauce, brown sugar, grated Asian pear, grated onion, minced garlic, grated ginger, sesame oil, mirin, black pepper, and water. Whisk everything together until the sugar is fully dissolved and the marinade is well combined.

instructions.title: Marinate the Short Ribs
instructions.text: Add the prepared short ribs to the marinade, ensuring each piece is fully coated. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, for the best flavor. Turn the ribs occasionally to ensure even marination.

instructions.title: Preheat Grill or Pan
instructions.text: When ready to cook, remove the ribs from the refrigerator 30 minutes prior to grilling. Preheat your outdoor grill to medium-high heat (about 400-450 degrees F) or a cast-iron grill pan on the stovetop over medium-high heat. Lightly oil the grates or pan to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Grill the Galbi
instructions.text: Place the marinated short ribs on the hot grill or pan. Grill for 3-5 minutes per side, depending on thickness and desired doneness. The ribs should have a nice char and be cooked through but still juicy. Avoid overcooking to keep them tender.

instructions.title: Rest and Garnish
instructions.text: Once cooked, remove the Galbi from the grill and let them rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring maximum tenderness. Slice them into individual rib pieces if desired, then transfer to a serving platter.

instructions.title: Serve Immediately
instructions.text: Garnish the grilled Galbi with toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions. Serve hot with steamed rice, kimchi, and other Korean side dishes (banchan) for a complete and authentic Korean BBQ experience.

tips: For extra tenderness, gently score the meat across the grain before marinating, being careful not to cut through the bones.

Serve Galbi with fresh lettuce leaves for wrapping, along with ssamjang (Korean dipping sauce) and sliced garlic, for an authentic Korean BBQ eating style.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the heart of Korea right from your kitchen with Galbi, the iconic Korean BBQ Short Ribs. This dish isn't just a meal; it's an experience, celebrated for its irresistible sweet and savory marinade that transforms humble beef short ribs into tender, caramelized masterpieces. Perfect for a family gathering, a special occasion, or simply an adventurous weeknight dinner, learning to make authentic Galbi at home is a rewarding endeavor that will undoubtedly impress your taste buds and those of your guests. Get ready to unlock the secrets to crafting one of the most beloved Korean dinner recipes.

## What is Galbi (Korean BBQ Short Ribs)?

Galbi, pronounced "kal-bee," literally means "rib" in Korean. When you hear "Galbi," it almost always refers to a dish made from beef short ribs, specifically a grilled marinated version. Often synonymous with the broader term Korean BBQ Short Ribs, Galbi stands out due to its distinctive marinade. This marinade is a carefully balanced blend of soy sauce, sugar (or other sweeteners like honey or rice syrup), garlic, ginger, sesame oil, and often a secret ingredient: grated Asian pear or apple. The fruit not only adds a subtle sweetness but also contains natural enzymes that tenderize the meat, ensuring a melt-in-your-mouth texture after grilling.

The preferred cut for Galbi is the "flanken-cut" short rib, which is cross-cut across the bone, resulting in thin, flat strips of meat with small pieces of bone attached. This allows for quick marinating and even cooking on a hot grill, creating those coveted crispy, charred edges while keeping the inside juicy. Galbi is a staple at Korean BBQ restaurants worldwide and a cherished dish in Korean homes, embodying the rich flavors and communal spirit of Korean cuisine.

## Ingredients You Need for Galbi

Creating delicious Galbi begins with gathering the right ingredients. The quality of your short ribs and the freshness of your marinade components will make all the difference.

For the Short Ribs:
*   3-4 lbs flanken-cut beef short ribs (approximately 1/2 to 3/4 inch thick)

For the Marinade:
*   1 cup soy sauce (low sodium preferred)
*   1/2 cup brown sugar (packed) or 1/3 cup honey/rice syrup
*   1/4 cup mirin (rice cooking wine)
*   1/4 cup sesame oil
*   1 head garlic, minced (about 8-10 cloves)
*   1-inch piece fresh ginger, grated
*   1 medium Asian pear or Fuji apple, grated (about 1/2 cup)
*   4 green onions, chopped (white and light green parts for marinade, green tops for garnish)
*   1 teaspoon black pepper
*   Optional: 1-2 tablespoons gochujang (Korean chili paste) for a spicy kick

## Step-by-Step Instructions to Make Galbi

Follow these steps carefully to ensure tender, flavorful Korean BBQ Short Ribs that will have everyone asking for seconds.

1.  **Prepare the Short Ribs:** Rinse the flanken-cut short ribs under cold water to remove any bone fragments. Pat them thoroughly dry with paper towels. If using English-cut short ribs, you'll need to butterfly them to a thinner, flatter cut (about 1/2-inch thick) to allow for better marinade penetration and quicker cooking. You can also lightly score the surface of the meat in a crosshatch pattern without cutting too deep.
2.  **Make the Marinade:** In a large bowl, combine the soy sauce, brown sugar (or honey/rice syrup), mirin, sesame oil, minced garlic, grated ginger, grated Asian pear (or apple), and black pepper. Whisk everything together until the sugar is fully dissolved. Stir in the chopped white and light green parts of the green onions. If you prefer a spicy Galbi, now is the time to whisk in the gochujang.
3.  **Marinate the Ribs:** Add the prepared short ribs to the marinade, ensuring each piece is fully submerged and coated. You can use a large bowl, a baking dish, or a large Ziploc bag for this. Cover the bowl or dish with plastic wrap, or seal the bag, and refrigerate for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight (12-24 hours) for maximum flavor and tenderness.
4.  **Grill the Galbi:** When ready to cook, preheat your grill to medium-high heat (about 400-450°F / 200-230°C). Lightly oil the grill grates to prevent sticking.
5.  **Cook the Ribs:** Place the marinated short ribs on the hot grill. Cook for 3-5 minutes per side, depending on thickness and desired doneness. You're looking for a beautiful caramelization and slight charring on the outside, and the meat should be cooked through but still juicy. Avoid overcooking, as this can make the ribs tough.
6.  **Rest and Serve:** Once cooked, transfer the Galbi to a cutting board and let them rest for 5 minutes before cutting into individual pieces along the bone or serving whole. Garnish with the remaining fresh green onion tops.

## Pro Tips for the Best Galbi Results

Achieving restaurant-quality Galbi at home is easier with a few insider tricks:

*   **Choose the Right Ribs:** Flanken-cut short ribs are ideal for traditional Korean BBQ Short Ribs. Their thin profile ensures the marinade permeates quickly and they cook evenly. If you can't find them, ask your butcher to cross-cut short ribs for you.
*   **Don't Skimp on Marination Time:** The longer the ribs marinate, the more flavorful and tender they will become. Overnight is truly the sweet spot, allowing the enzymes from the fruit to work their magic on the connective tissues.
*   **The Power of Fruit:** Asian pear or apple is not just for flavor; it's a natural tenderizer. The enzymes break down tough meat fibers. However, be careful not to marinate for more than 24 hours with fruit, as it can make the meat mushy.
*   **High Heat is Key for Grilling:** A hot grill creates a beautiful sear and caramelization, locking in the juices. Don't overcrowd the grill; cook in batches if necessary to maintain consistent heat.
*   **Rest Your Meat:** Just like any grilled meat, letting your Galbi rest for a few minutes after cooking allows the juices to redistribute, resulting in a more tender and moist bite.

## Serving Suggestions for Korean Short Ribs

Enjoying Korean Short Ribs is an experience that extends beyond just the meat itself. Traditional Korean meals are often served family-style with an array of side dishes that complement the main course beautifully.

*   **Steamed Rice:** A bowl of freshly steamed white rice is essential to balance the rich flavors of the Galbi.
*   **Lettuce Wraps (Ssam):** Offer crisp lettuce leaves (like red leaf, green leaf, or romaine) or perilla leaves (kkaennip) for wrapping the meat.
*   **Ssamjang:** This savory, spicy dipping sauce, a blend of gochujang and doenjang (fermented soybean paste), is a must-have for lettuce wraps.
*   **Kimchi:** No Korean meal is complete without kimchi! Napa cabbage kimchi is a classic, but other varieties like radish kimchi (kkakdugi) are also excellent.
*   **Banchan (Side Dishes):** A selection of small Korean side dishes such as pickled radish, seasoned bean sprouts, cucumber salad, or spinach namul will elevate your meal.
*   **Drinks:** Pair your Galbi with a refreshing Korean beer (like Hite or Cass) or a shot of soju for an authentic dining experience.

## Variations and Substitutions for Galbi

This beloved Korean BBQ Short Ribs recipe is incredibly versatile, allowing for delicious variations and substitutions to suit your preferences or what you have on hand.

*   **Spicy Galbi:** For those who love a kick, increase the amount of gochujang in the marinade, or add a pinch of gochugaru (Korean chili flakes).
*   **Pork Galbi (Dwaeji Galbi):** While beef is traditional, you can easily adapt this marinade for pork ribs. Pork short ribs or pork butt cut into thin slices work wonderfully and offer a different flavor profile.
*   **Alternative Tenderizers:** If you don't have Asian pear or apple, a small amount of kiwi (about 1/4 of a kiwi per pound of meat) can be used, but be very cautious as kiwi is a powerful tenderizer and can turn meat mushy if left too long (no more than 2-3 hours). Pineapple juice is another option but also potent.
*   **Cooking Indoors:** Don't have a grill? You can still make fantastic Korean BBQ Short Ribs! Use a cast-iron grill pan on your stovetop or broil the ribs in your oven. For broiler, place ribs on a foil-lined baking sheet and broil for 3-4 minutes per side, keeping a close eye to prevent burning. Ensure good ventilation for indoor cooking.
*   **Vegetarian Option:** While not Galbi, the marinade can be adapted for firm tofu or hearty mushrooms (like king oyster mushrooms) for a delicious vegetarian Korean-inspired dish.

Mastering Galbi is a culinary triumph that brings the heart of Korean dining to your home. The rich, complex flavors of these marinated and grilled Korean BBQ Short Ribs are truly unforgettable. So, gather your ingredients, fire up the grill, and prepare to create a memorable feast that celebrates the joy of homemade Korean cuisine.
